questions.question: 实现一个支持 SET/GET/DELETE 的内存 key-value 存储，然后加上 BEGIN/COMMIT/ROLLBACK 事务，并支持嵌套事务。
questions.questionEn: Build an in-memory key-value store with SET/GET/DELETE, then add transactions with BEGIN/COMMIT/ROLLBACK, including nested transactions.

questions.question: 写一个迭代器类，惰性地展平任意嵌套的列表（列表里套列表或整数）：不能用生成器，状态必须显式维护。
questions.questionEn: Write an iterator class that lazily flattens an arbitrarily nested list of lists/integers: no generators, explicit state.

questions.question: 这是一个小型 LLM 推理引擎里的调度器类。其中一个方法 \_admit_requests 只是桩：没有规格说明、没有 docstring、没有测试。说说你最初三十分钟会怎么做。
questions.questionEn: Here is a scheduler class from a small LLM inference engine. One method, \_admit_requests, is a stub: no spec, no docstring, no tests. Walk me through your first thirty minutes.

questions.topicName: 推理、服务与 GPU 性能
questions.question: 估算在 128k 上下文下服务一个 70B 级别模型所需的 KV cache 显存。如果放不下，你会怎么办？
questions.questionEn: Estimate the KV-cache memory to serve a 70B-class model at 128k context. What do you do when it doesn't fit?

sources.title: LLM 中的 KV Cache 是什么？

questions.topicName: 推理、服务与 GPU 性能
questions.question: 为一个按 token 而非请求数计费的 LLM API 设计限流器。
questions.questionEn: Design a rate limiter for an LLM API where cost scales with tokens, not requests.

questions.question: 你在数万张 GPU 上训练，硬件不断故障。如何让 goodput 保持在高位？
questions.questionEn: You're training on tens of thousands of GPUs and hardware fails constantly. How do you keep goodput high?

questions.question: 大规模预训练任务训练中途出现 loss 尖峰。说说你的排查过程。
questions.questionEn: Loss spikes mid-run on a large pretraining job. Walk me through your debugging process.

questions.question: 为 web 规模的预训练语料设计去重流水线，而且必须以流式方式运行。
questions.questionEn: Design a deduplication pipeline for a web-scale pretraining corpus. It has to run as a streaming process.

questions.question: 为一个面向消费者的聊天机器人设计服务栈，它要在社交媒体实时数据流上做实时搜索。
questions.questionEn: Design the serving stack for a consumer chatbot with real-time search over a social-media firehose.

questions.question: 你有四个小时来构建并演示一个可用的 AI 产品。你会怎么分配这四小时？
questions.questionEn: You have four hours to build and demo a working AI-powered product. How do you spend them?
